title: The Difficult Marriage Between Trust and Respect
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This piece unpacks the often-conflated relationship between trust and respect, arguing the two are related but distinct and can exist independently of one another. Trust is about believing in someone's integrity and consistency; respect is about admiring their abilities or qualities - meaning it's entirely possible to trust someone's character while doubting their competence, or vice versa. The article notes that treating people respectfully tends to build trust, and extending trust tends to build respect, creating a reinforcing loop, but the two don't move in lockstep. It also observes an asymmetry: respect can grow incrementally with demonstrated skill, while trust, once broken, is far harder to rebuild and behaves more like an all-or-nothing state.
